reviewer: root, independently reviewing the helper and multipart changes authored by subagents; the fitting-batch tests were separately reviewed by static_lookup_oracle

conclusions.result: No additional defect found. The helper preserves exact block/receipt/terminal checks and supplies checked request-local L1 history to the existing executor. Parent trie, position-bound native identity, import bytes, fork rules and PREVRANDAO are validated. It accepts no caller-supplied prefix state root.

The deployed L1 genesis or existing public preset reaches the helper, with a manager commitment read at the original post block. RPC storage only locates a bounded header range. Public preset loading cannot turn an evidence string into an arbitrary file path. Private Gnosis profiles remain explicitly unsupported by this helper.

The revised assertions distinguish retained ordinary settlement from a capacity fallback and preserve one-post/range/blob/receipt checks. Fullness additionally checks the posted root update, success event, retained checkpoint, canonical terminal and both replayed applications. No runtime policy change.

The terminal is fixed once and covers all receipts and the minimum history. The last application deliberately arrives beyond the old boundary, preventing timing-dependent accidental coverage. Every bounded proof, final actual-parent part, negative evidence check and cold replay remains.

Only the example required-features contract changes; chain-spec was already active in both producer and archive dependency graphs. Cargo.lock, node, follower, signer, core pin, RPC and on-chain contracts are unchanged since the verified CI runtime candidate.

remaining_limits: The final corrected helper is a locally built debug-profile executable; the live node/follower/signer are the verified prior CI release payload. The next CI run must establish the new published helper/test payload.
Two missing-proxy live scenarios did not reach their intended terminal queue oracle; 26 unsupported signer-profile scenarios remain excluded. Core Anvil64/64 is separate evidence.
No Nethermind server was available; conformance vectors do not prove integration with that implementation.
Inherited dependency advisories remain an integration blocker; no waiver or dependency upgrade is included.
The shared-host OOM incident and the limits of the process-recovery observation remain recorded.
